lines.trans: Look at Rami's cutting board, Salma—every carrot cube is identical!
Even cubes cook at the exact same speed, brother. Basic physics!
Laugh all you want, Ziad, that is the neatest soup prep my kitchen has ever seen!
Pot is warm with olive oil—onions and carrots going in now?
Yes! Stir three minutes until sweet, then add red lentils and hot broth.
Need the courtyard thyme and parsley next, Chef?
Two fresh sprigs tied with string, plus one pinch of salt at the end.
Listening to soup simmer in a stone kitchen beats city traffic any day.
Funny—three years ago we argued on the phone, and today we make soup together.
Remind me never to wait three years to call you again, Ziad.
All right, brothers, save the tears—my bread timer is ringing!
Oven mitts on! Eight crusty loaves coming out hot!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of قطّع (to chop into pieces); لوح تقطيع is a cutting board.

examples.trans: We used the word تقطيع.
This is another تقطيع.

meanings.note: Male given name belonging to Ziad's younger brother, the quiet architect.

examples.trans: We used the word رامي.
This is another رامي.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Female given name belonging to the café's morning baker.

examples.trans: We used the word سلمى.
This is another سلمى.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Used for ice cubes (مكعب تلج), sugar cubes, and diced vegetables.

examples.text: دوق الشوربة وشوف إذا بدها كمان مكعب جزر.
examples.trans: Taste the soup and see if it needs another cube of carrot.

examples.text: لفينا مكعبات التلج بمنشفة قطن نضيفة.
examples.trans: We wrapped the ice cubes in a clean cotton towel.

meanings.note: Collective noun جزر ('carrots') with singulative جزرة ('one carrot').

examples.text: فرمنا الجزر والبصل لمكعبات صغيرة ومتساوية.
examples.trans: We diced the carrots and onions into small, even cubes.

examples.text: الجزر المشوي بيعطي الشوربة حلاوة طبيعية.
examples.trans: Roasted carrots give the soup a natural sweetness.

قد.gloss: as much as; the size of

meanings.en: as much as; the size of
meanings.note: Expresses equal amount or degree: قدنا مرتين ('twice as much as us'), قد ما بقدر ('as much as I can').

examples.trans: Tariq is twice as curious as we are!
I tried to smile as much as I could!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضبط, بيضبط).

examples.trans: Set the alarm for six, Tariq.
The plan worked out one hundred percent!

meanings.note: Form VI active participle meaning 'even in thickness, spacing, or size'.

examples.text: طبقة الدهان طلعت ناعمة ومتساوية من أول لوح لآخره.
examples.trans: The coat of paint came out smooth and even from one end of the panel to the other.

examples.text: قطعنا العجينة لدوائر متساوية لصواني التارت.
examples.trans: We cut the dough into even circles for the tart pans.

meanings.note: Key Jordanian kitchen verb استوى meaning 'to become cooked/done' (for food) or 'ripe' (for fruit).

examples.trans: We used the word استوى.
This is another استوى.

meanings.note: Unvocalised نفس covers nafas ('breath': خد نفس عميق take a deep breath) and nafs ('same': نفس الشي the same thing).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Adverbial form of تمام meaning 'precisely' or 'completely'.

examples.trans: We used the word تماماً.
This is another تماماً.

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Colloquial spelling of فيزياء (physics), dropping the final hamza.

examples.trans: We used the word فيزيا.
This is another فيزيا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.
The problem is minor and easy to fix.

meanings.note: Everyday Form I verb (بضحك / ضحك) meaning 'to laugh' or 'grin playfully'.

examples.text: ليش عم بتضحك لجيبة الجاكيت تبعتك؟
examples.trans: Why are you grinning at your coat pocket?

examples.text: ضحكنا كلنا لما شفنا النظارة على جبينه.
examples.trans: We all laughed when we saw the glasses on his forehead.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Core Levantine word for 'want', inflected with pronoun suffixes rather than verb prefixes.

examples.trans: We used the word بد.
This is another بد.

meanings.note: Male given name, here referring to Rami's older brother.

examples.trans: We used the word زياد.
This is another زياد.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation of هذا ('this/that').

examples.trans: We used the word هادا.
This is another هادا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مرتبة, plural: مرتبين).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting right away.
Neat pencil sketches.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of حضّر ('to prepare'). Plural: تحضيرات.

examples.trans: Coffee prep takes ten minutes.
All preparations for the party are ready.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: شوربات.

examples.trans: Here is a cup of hot vegetable soup.
Hot soup is wonderful on a rainy day.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Life is sweet with kind people.
Never in my life have I seen a prettier view.

meanings.note: Standard Levantine kitchen noun for a cooking pot or saucepan.

examples.trans: We used the word طنجرة.
This is another طنجرة.

meanings.note: Intransitive verb سخن ('to heat up / become warm'), agreeing with الطنجرة.

examples.trans: We used the word سَخِن.
This is another سَخِن.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Cooking oil (زيت زيتون 'olive oil') or machine/hinge oil.

examples.text: حطينا نقطتين زيت على كل مفصلة حديد.
examples.trans: We put two drops of oil on every iron hinge.

examples.text: شوربة العدس بتطلع أطيب مع رشة زيت زيتون.
examples.trans: Lentil soup tastes even better with a drizzle of olive oil.

meanings.note: Collective noun for olives, iconic to Jordanian tables and courtyards.

examples.text: فطور الصبح ما بيكمل بدون زيت وزيتون أخضر.
examples.trans: Morning breakfast isn't complete without olive oil and green olives.

examples.text: شجرة الزيتون بآخر الحارة عمرها مية سنة.
examples.trans: The olive tree at the end of the lane is a hundred years old.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: Let us bring the suitcase down into the light.
Let me lower my glasses from my forehead!

meanings.note: Collective noun for onions; a single onion is بصلة.

examples.trans: We used the word بصل.
This is another بصل.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for both casual 'yes / yeah' and 'oh! / ah!' upon noticing something.

examples.trans: Oh, the door opened! Thank you.
Yes, eight rooms and eight keys.

meanings.note: Form II verb حرّك means 'to move' or 'to stir' ingredients.

examples.trans: We used the word حرّك.
This is another حرّك.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Common Levantine conjunction meaning 'until' or 'so that'.

examples.trans: We used the word لحتى.
This is another لحتى.

meanings.note: Verb حلي means 'to become sweet' (used for caramelizing onions and carrots).

examples.trans: We used the word حلي.
This is another حلي.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'then, next, afterwards' (وبعدين 'and then').

examples.trans: Lift the handle first, and then push.
Have some tea and then we will talk.

meanings.note: Hollow verb (يزيد / بزيد). Used both transitively ('to add something') and intransitively ('to grow').

examples.text: كل يوم بزيد ملاحظة جديدة بالدفتر.
examples.trans: Every day I add a new note to the ledger.
The wind picked up in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Collective noun; شوربة عدس ('golden lentil soup' with lemon and olive oil) is a beloved Jordanian staple.

examples.text: شوربة العدس مع عصرة ليمون أطيب غدا بالشتا.
examples.trans: Lentil soup with a squeeze of lemon is the best lunch on a rainy day.

examples.text: سلمى غسلت العدس الأصفر وحطته عالنار.
examples.trans: Salma rinsed the yellow lentils and set them on the stove.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: Everyday kitchen word for broth, stock, or sauce.

examples.trans: We used the word مرقة.
This is another مرقة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: Fresh wild thyme (or the dried herb blend), an iconic Levantine culinary herb.

examples.trans: We used the word زعتر.
This is another زعتر.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for parsley.

examples.trans: We used the word بقدونس.
This is another بقدونس.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used across modern Jordanian kitchens and cafés for both male and female head chefs.

examples.text: الدفتر جاهز يا شيف سلمى، بشو نبلش؟
examples.trans: The clipboard is ready, Chef Salma—what do we start with?

examples.text: الشيف ذاق الشوربة وابتسم من أول معلقة.
examples.trans: The chef tasted the soup and smiled from the very first spoonful.

meanings.note: Slender climbing stem or root of jasmine, mint, or ivy ('iriq, pl. 'ruuq).

examples.text: حطيت عرق نعنع أخضر بكاسة الشاي السخن.
examples.trans: I put a sprig of fresh green mint into the glass of hot tea.

examples.text: عرق اللبلاب طلع عالحيط الحجر لحد الشباك.
examples.trans: The ivy vine climbed up the stone wall right to the window.

meanings.note: Invariable colloquial adjective (from Persian tāza via Ottoman Turkish) used for fresh bread, fruit, and herbs.

examples.text: خبز سلمى طازة وسخن كل صبح.
examples.trans: Salma's bread is fresh and hot every morning.

examples.text: اشترينا ليمون طازة ونعنع أخضر من السوق.
examples.trans: We bought fresh lemons and green mint from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مربوطة, plural: مربوطين).

examples.trans: There is a paper tag tied to the handle.
The red ribbon is tied securely.

meanings.note: Noun for thread, twine, or kitchen string.

examples.trans: I have a long string.
I tied it with a string.

meanings.note: Instance noun from رش ('sprinkle/spray'): رشة ملح = 'a pinch of salt'.

examples.text: الشوربة بدها بس رشة ملح وعصرة ليمون.
examples.trans: The soup just needs a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon.

examples.text: حطي رشة قرفة ناعمة فوق الفنجان.
examples.trans: Put a light sprinkle of ground cinnamon on top of the cup.

meanings.note: Essential kitchen noun; ملح بحر = 'sea salt'.

examples.text: إوعك تخربط بين مرتبان السكر ومرتبان الملح!
examples.trans: Don't ever mix up the sugar jar and the salt jar!

examples.text: حطيت نص معلقة ملح بالعجين قبل الخبز.
examples.trans: I added half a spoonful of salt to the dough before baking.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) of سمع ('hear/listen').

examples.text: سماع الموسيقى بهالغرفة الهادية بيرح البال.
examples.trans: Listening to music in this quiet room puts the mind at ease.
We were delighted to hear the good news.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday kitchen verb for boiling liquids.

examples.trans: We used the word غلى.
This is another غلى.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حجار.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حلوة, plural: حلوين).

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: In everyday Amman speech, أزمة most often means heavy city traffic.

examples.trans: Downtown traffic at noon is slow.
We arrived ten minutes before the traffic jam.

meanings.note: In Amman, وسط البلد or simply البلد refers to downtown Amman.

examples.trans: We went down to downtown in the morning.
Town is quiet on Friday.

meanings.note: In questions أي means 'which?' (أي علبة؟ 'which tin?'); in conditionals/negatives it means 'any' (أي شي 'anything').

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!

meanings.note: As an adjective غريب / غريبة means 'strange, odd'; as a noun (plural غرباء) it means 'stranger(s)'.

examples.trans: I heard a strange metallic knock at night.
Why would he leave his bag with strangers?

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخانق, بيتخانق).

examples.trans: We used to argue over the corner piece!
We fell out over selling the old house.

meanings.note: Spoken contraction of على التلفون ('on the telephone').

examples.trans: We used the word تلفون.
This is another تلفون.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'together'.

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
We drank morning coffee together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بذكر, بيذكر).

examples.trans: Do not remind him of the old mix-up!
Remind me of the bus time tomorrow.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتصل, بيتصل).

examples.trans: Call the lost-and-found office right away.
You called us on Tuesday.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرات.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Ubiquitous Jordanian interjection meaning 'enough / okay / that's it!'.

examples.trans: We used the word خلص.
This is another خلص.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخفف, بيخفف).

examples.text: الخشب بيخفف الصدى عن حجر الشارع.
examples.trans: The wood softens the echo off the street stone.
We dimmed the light in the courtyard in the evening.

meanings.note: Broken plural of دمعة (teardrop).

examples.trans: We used the word دمعة.
This is another دمعة.

meanings.note: Kitchen or oven timer (from وقت 'time').

examples.text: عيرت المؤقت على تمنطاعشر دقيقة للتارت.
examples.trans: I set the timer for eighteen minutes for the tarts.

examples.text: أبو طارق عينه عالمؤقت عشان ما يتحمر الخبز زيادة.
examples.trans: Abu Tariq keeps his eye on the timer so the bread doesn't over-brown.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Verb رنّ means 'to ring' (for a bell, phone, or timer).

examples.trans: We used the word رنّ.
This is another رنّ.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلبس, بيلبس).

examples.text: أنا أكيد ما بلبس مقاس أربعة وأربعين!
examples.trans: I certainly do not wear size forty-four!

examples.text: لبس معطفه قبل ما يطلع بالمطر.
examples.trans: He put on his coat before going out in the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for gloves or oven mitts (literally 'palms').

examples.trans: We used the word كفّ.
This is another كفّ.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Broken plural of رغيف, the classic Arabic word for a loaf of bread.

examples.trans: We used the word رغيف.
This is another رغيف.

meanings.note: Favorite Levantine food word for crusty fresh bread or crisp pastry.

examples.text: الخبز طلع من الفرن سخن ومقرمش.
examples.trans: The bread came out of the oven hot and crusty.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز المقرمشة أطيب إشي بالتارت.
examples.trans: The crisp almond crust is the best part of the tart.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.
